newsitem.title: USA: Sex convictions of Mass. day-care workers restored.
newsitem.headline: Sex convictions of Mass. day-care workers restored.

text.p: Massachusetts' highest court on Monday reinstated the convictions of a mother and daughter, and denied a new trial for the son in a family accused of molesting more than 40 children at a day-care centre they operated.

The Supreme Judicial Court, in a 6-to-1 decision, rejected the family's argument that they were denied their constitutional right to a face-to-face confrontation with their accusers, some 14 children who testified the family abused them in their Malden, Massachusetts, day-care centre during the 1980s.

Violet Amirault, 74, and her daughter, Cheryl Amirault LeFave, who have been free since August 1995 when a lower court judge granted their motion for a new trial, will be sent back to prison, prosecutors said. The pair served eight years of their eight-to-20 year sentence when they were granted a new trial.
Gerald Amirault, who was tried separately and received a sentence of 30-to-40 years, has remained in prison.
The Amiraults were twice convicted of sexually molesting about 40 children, ages 3 to 6 years old, at the Fells Acres day care centre which the family ran.
The Amiraults maintained their innocence since the allegations first arose.

"I have 12 more years to do for a crime I never committed," a teary-eyed Mrs. Amirault told reporters. "I'm having a hard time comprehending what is an on-going battle my family has faced. There was never a crime committed at Fells Acres...There was never any shred of evidence that any harm was done to these children."

She then asked both the president and Gov. William Weld, who has the power, to commute the sentences to time served. A spokeman for Weld said the governor was waiting to read the Supreme Judicial Court's opinions.
"Prison is very difficult for the guilty," Mrs. Amirault said, "and very difficult for the innocent."
Prosecutors said they would quickly file a motion to return the pair to prison.
Cheryl Amirault LeFave told reporters at her lawyer's offices, "We absolutely destroyed and we're not ready to go back to prison."
